messages.content: i finished my book this afternoon, and now i keep trying to open it even though there is nothing left to read.
you spent time with that story, so it may still be part of what you want to do with your evening. would you like to talk about the end or choose what to read next?
i want to talk about the end.
tell me what happened at the end and what you thought about it. i do not know the story yet.
the girl went home, but the friend she made stayed in the village. i wanted them to leave together.
they went to different places, but you wanted them to go together. what did you like about the two friends?
ask that question simply.
what did you like about the two friends?
they listened to each other. i liked that more than the journey.
you liked how they listened to each other more than where they went.
say that in fewer words.
you liked how they listened most.
write a story with two keys and one door. the child should learn which key to use by asking, not by already knowing.

a child finds two keys in a small container. one is long and one is short. she wants to open the garden door, but she does not know which key is for it. she asks her grandfather. he says that the short key is for the garden, while the long one is for another door inside the house. she takes the short key and opens the garden door. before going out, she puts the long key back in the container.
give just the part about her not knowing which key to use.
she wants to open the garden door, but she does not know which key is for it.
why did she not take both keys outside?
she only needed the short one for the garden door. the long key was for another door, so she put it back where she found it.
can we say she knows what every key in the house opens now?
no. she learned about those two keys. that does not tell her about every other key in the house.
add a question she could ask before leaving.
where should i put the garden key when i come back?
my friend told me about a hard day. i started telling them what to do, but they wanted me to listen first.
you can slow down and ask them to tell you more. listening first can help you understand what kind of help they want, if they want help at all.
what can i say now with a short kind reply?
you could say: i went too fast with ideas. i would like to hear the rest before talking about what to do.
that answer works. i wanted a short kind reply.
then you can use that reply and give your friend room to speak. you do not have to choose what they should do before hearing the whole story.
say the last idea simply.
you do not have to choose what your friend should do right away. first, listen to what they want to tell you.
what if they later ask for my idea?
then you can give an idea using the details they gave. you might ask whether it would help, rather than saying you know the only right answer.
say that in fewer words.
give an idea and ask whether it would help.
my brother took a book from the shelf and put it on the table. later, i moved it from the table to my desk. where is it now?
it is on your desk, from the last move you told me about.
answer with just the place.
on your desk.
my brother says he cannot find it on the table. help me tell him where it is without saying he lost it.
i moved the book from the table to my desk. it is there now.
why not say you put it in the wrong place?
you did not say that the table was a wrong place for the book. your brother put it there, and you moved it later. the message can explain the change without saying he did something wrong.
say that simply.
the book is not on the table because you moved it. you can tell him that without saying he did something wrong.
now he takes it from my desk. do we know where he puts it?
no. you only said that he takes it. we need another detail to know its next place.
i have work in the morning and a free evening. i want to leave the evening open but still remember one call i need to make.
you can keep one clear task in the evening without choosing every hour. write down the call and leave the rest of the time open.
the call is to my aunt. she asked me to call after dinner.
then your note can say: call my aunt after dinner. that gives you the person and a time without making a whole plan for the evening.
what if i have dinner at a different time from her?
did she mean after her dinner or after yours? asking can help you choose a time that works.
give me the question to ask her.
when you say after dinner, do you mean after your dinner or mine?
she wants me to call after her dinner at seven. write the note again.
call my aunt after seven, when she has finished dinner.
write my last answer simply.
she wants me to call after her dinner at seven.
can you answer where is the book with the book is on the table?
yes. that answer gives the place asked for in the question.
what if i answer the book is blue?
that gives its color, rather than where it is. it may be true, but it does not answer the question about place.
can an answer be true and still not answer the question?
yes. a fact can be correct but about something different from what was asked. a useful reply should give the information the person asked for.
explain that last part simply.
a useful reply should give the information the person asked for. a true sentence about another detail may not do that.
ask me a place question about a cup.
where is the cup?
it is white.
that gives the color. where did you put the cup?
on the shelf.
now you have answered the question about place. the cup is on the shelf.
the garden near my house has a table now. i hope people will use it for reading.
that could give people a place to sit with a book. have you tried sitting there yourself yet?
not yet. i saw it through the garden door while walking past.
then you know the table is there, but not yet how it feels to sit at it. you could try it on a day when you have time.
i want to bring my sister, but she likes drawing more than reading.
she could draw while you read if the space works for both. using a table together does not mean doing the same thing.
say that with fewer words.
you can use the same table for different things. she can draw while you read.
what should i ask her?
would you like to sit in the garden with me? you could draw while i read.
should i say it will be quiet for sure?
only if you know that. you have seen the table, but you have not said what the garden is like when people are using it.
write a story about a child who reads only the first line of a note and gets the wrong idea.

a child finds a note on the kitchen table. the first line says: please leave the book. she thinks she should not take her book to school. then her brother asks her to read the next line too. it says: on my desk before you go. the whole message asks her to put a book on the desk, rather than leave all her books at home. she reads the note again and asks which book her mother wants.
why does the next line change the meaning?
the first line does not give the whole request. the next line gives the place and time for leaving the book. reading only part can leave out important context.
can we say the first line was false?
no. it was part of a longer message. the problem was that she did not read the whole request. the first line was not false by itself.
say that last part simply.
the problem was that she did not read the whole request. the first line was not false by itself.
write a useful question for the child to ask.
which book should i put on your desk before i go?
i spent a week at my cousin house and want to send a short thank you message. we cooked, read, and walked together.
you could write: thank you for having me for the week. i enjoyed cooking, reading, and walking with you.
cousin house is not good grammar. how could i say my first sentence without that?
i spent a week at the house of my cousin and want to send a short thank you message.
i want it to sound less like a list. keep only the general idea.
thank you for having me for the week. i enjoyed our time together and was happy to visit.
add that i got home last night.
i got home last night. thank you for having me for the week. i enjoyed our time together and was happy to visit.
does got home mean i am still on the journey?
no. got home says that you were home. it puts that part of the journey in the past.
say that simply.
no. you were home last night. the sentence does not say you are still on the journey.
my table has room for six books. does that tell me six people can sit there?
no. room for books is different from room for people. you need other information to know how many people can sit at the table.
what should i look at?
you could look at the space around the table, the number of chairs, and whether each person would have room to sit and use the table.
write a short story where someone learns this before asking friends to read there.

a girl puts six books on a small table and thinks six friends can read there. her brother brings two chairs and sees that there is no space for more. they choose to use the large table in another room instead. then the group can sit with room for their books too.
did the number of books change the size of the table?
no. the books being on the table did not make the table larger. the girl had to think about the people and chairs as well.
can they still use the small table for something?
yes. they could keep the other books there while reading at the large table.
say it with fewer words.
they could put other books on the small table.
i found a sentence i do not understand, but i want to finish the page before asking about it.
you can keep a note of the sentence and read to the end of the page. the next part may give context that helps. if it is still not clear, return to it later.
say it simply.
read to the end of the page, then return to the sentence. the next part may help you understand it.
what if i forget the question?
write a short note on another piece of paper before reading more. you do not need to write in the book.
give just the first sentence.
write a short note on another piece of paper before reading more.
i finished the page, and now the sentence is clear. do i still have to ask?
no. if you understand it now, you can keep reading. you may ask if you want to check your understanding, but you do not have to ask just because you had a question before.
say the last part simply.
you can keep reading if the sentence is clear now. you do not have to ask just because you had a question before.
my friend sat with me while i finished a hard piece of work. they did not do the work, but it helped to have them there.
then their help was being with you, rather than doing the task for you. you can thank them for that time without saying they wrote or made anything.
help me say it.
thank you for sitting with me while i worked. having you there helped me keep going.
what if they say they did nothing?
you did not do the task, but your time was important to me. i wanted someone there, and you stayed.
keep only the first sentence.
you did not do the task, but your time was important to me.
can i ask them to do that every time i work?
you can ask, but they may not always have time. it can help to make one specific request rather than asking them to be there for every task.
give me a request for tomorrow only.
would you have time to sit with me for a little while when i work tomorrow?
i read two stories about a person leaving home. can they still be very different stories?
yes. both people can leave home, but they may go for different reasons and have different things happen later.
say that simply.
yes. leaving home can be part of two different stories.
make that answer longer, with the word reasons.
both people can leave home, but they may have different reasons. what happens later can also be different.
in one, the person wants to visit a friend. in the other, the person wants to be alone.
then the stories already give different reasons. one person wants time with someone, while the other wants time without other people.
can both end with the person going home?
yes. the same end place does not mean that the whole journey or the feeling about it was the same.
write a simple question i can ask about both stories.
what changed for each person before going home?
i put my drawing tools in an old container that used to hold food. is it a new container now?
it is the same container with a new use. changing what you put inside does not make it a different object.
write a small story about a child choosing a place for drawing tools.

a child has drawing tools on the table. her father asks where she will keep them when she is done. she finds an empty container in the kitchen. he says it used to hold food, but it is clean and free to use. she puts her tools inside and carries it to the desk. now she knows where to look when she wants to draw again.
make the story shorter.
a child has drawing tools on the table. her father asks where she will keep them when she is done. she finds an empty container that is clean and free to use, then puts her tools inside.
what changed in the story?
the container is being used for drawing tools instead of food. the tools also have a place where the child can find them again.
did the container grow larger?
no. nothing in the story says that its size changed.
four people talked about a book. the last person gave the answer to a question. does that mean the other people did not know it?
no. someone answering last does not tell us what everyone else knew. other people may have known the answer without saying it.
can you make the question simple?
four people talked about a book. one gave the answer. did only that person know it?
what if the other three said they did not know?
then you have more information. those three said they did not know, while the person answering gave an answer. what each person said gives more information than only knowing who answered last.
explain that in fewer words.
use what each person said, rather than only the order they said it in.
give one sentence with said.
what each person said gives more information than only knowing who answered last.
can i know the last answer was correct just because everyone was quiet after it?
no. people being quiet does not make an answer correct. you would need to check the answer itself.
help me plan a quiet afternoon. i want to read in the garden and call my sister after that.
you could read first, then call your sister when you are ready to come inside. leave some time between the two if you want a break.
she just sent a message saying she is free now but busy later.
then you can change the order if you want to talk with her today. call first while she is free, then read in the garden later.
keep just the last sentence.
call first while she is free, then read in the garden later.
does that mean the first plan was wrong?
no. it used the information you had at the time. your sister gave a new detail that made a different order useful.
i do not want to call today after all. i want to read and leave the call for tomorrow.
then your afternoon can be for reading. you can ask your sister whether there is a time tomorrow when you are both free.
write that message to her.
i am going to read this afternoon. would there be a good time for us to talk tomorrow?
